title: Grateful Dead Live at Oregon County Fair on 1982-08-28

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a scorching August‑28‑1982 Oregon Country Fair show with Jerry’s searing Black Peter and the debut of West LA Fadeaway.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean soundboard source that, while a touch low in level for some listeners, delivers plenty of bottom end and clarity. The performance is high‑energy – new tunes like West LA Fadeaway shine alongside classics such as Black Peter, Althea and China Rider, with Jerry’s guitar work and Brent’s keyboards standing out. Overall the show is remembered as a quintessential “dust‑and‑sun” Dead experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Over two dozen enthusiastic reviews (mostly 5‑star) praise both the music and the recording; technical comments are minor, while standout performances dominate, justifying a high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear soundboard mix with good instrument separation; some listeners note slightly low overall levels but no major drop‑outs or distortion.

poor_songs: Bertha (lyric flub noted by one reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A blend of new material and beloved classics, with the first set moving through country‑rock tunes into a punchy second set where jams flow freely; dust‑and‑sun ambience adds to the live feel.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for searing guitar leads on Black Peter, tight leads throughout, and creative use of his envelope filter/turnarounds.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as a “blurring” bass that vibrated the venue, strong low‑end presence.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for intense, fiery vocals (“Bob songs”) and solid rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland highlighted as “hot”, delivering straight‑ahead piano, organ swells, and driving funk textures on West LA Fadeaway.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey (and Bill) praised for being “on fire” with a powerful bottom end and energetic drumming throughout.
